question: MCI versus normal controls from baseline structural T1 MRI in clinic older adults. P-50: 24 MCI / 22 NC from the Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital neurology clinic. P-99: 145 MCI / 62 HC from a Moscow memory clinic. The task, the population class (clinic patients with MCI against cognitively normal controls) and the channel (MRI) are the same. The cohorts, MCI criteria, features, scanners and CV schemes differ; the rule allows these and they are listed as candidate explanations.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (0.89 vs 0.73) and ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (0.89 vs 0.735), both from internal cross-validation.

figures.P-99: Accuracy 0.73 +- 0.059 and ROC-AUC 0.735 +- 0.076 (RBF SVC, 10-fold CV, n = 207, Table 1). The +- values are fold standard deviations, not 95% intervals, so intervals are derived. Recall 0.796 for MCI and 0.583 for controls give about 115/145 + 36/62 = 151/207 = 0.729. Wilson 95%: z^2/n = 0.0186; centre = 0.725; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.729*0.271/207 + 3.8416/(4*207^2))/1.0186 = 0.060; interval [0.665, 0.785]. Hanley-McNeil for AUC 0.735 with 145 MCI / 62 HC: Q1 = 0.581; Q2 = 0.623; SE^2 = [0.1948 + 144*0.0408 + 61*0.0825]/8990 = 11.10/8990 = 0.00124; SE = 0.035; interval [0.666, 0.804]. Even if the fold SDs are used as the spread (0.73 +- 1.96*0.059 = [0.614, 0.846]; 0.735 +- 1.96*0.076 = [0.586, 0.884]), P-50's 0.89 still lies outside both.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-50 also reports single feature sets (subcortical volume/shape 0.78, sulcal depth/gyrification 0.84, Table 5), but these are its own VBM/SBM features, not P-99's FreeSurfer set. P-99 reports six classifiers (0.637-0.73 accuracy) on its FreeSurfer features, but no linear SVM on P-50's features and no subsample like P-50's. Neither paper reports a result under the other's condition, so nothing in either paper closes the gap.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the Section 3.5 exclusion. P-50's best is accuracy 0.89 / AUC 0.89 (below 0.97), though from LOOCV on 46 people with no external cohort. P-99's best is 0.73 / 0.735. Checked against Table 5 of P-50 and Table 1 of P-99.

candidate_explanations.difference: Feature derivation: P-50 builds its classifier features from the regions where MCI and NC differed in its own group analysis of the same 46 people. The paper does not say this selection was repeated inside each LOOCV fold, which can inflate cross-validated accuracy.
candidate_explanations.quote: Discriminative features were derived from differential imaging indicators of cortical and subcortical morphology alterations.

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size and class balance: 46 participants (24/22) evaluated by LOOCV, against 207 participants (145/62, imbalanced) evaluated by 10-fold CV.
candidate_explanations.quote: First, the sample size of the study was relatively small, and more subjects should be recruited in the future study to draw more accurate conclusions.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition: P-50 requires a memory complaint, MMSE 25-26 and MoCA 19-25. P-99 uses an ICD-10 F06.7 diagnosis in patients over 65.
candidate_explanations.quote: Patients over the age of 65 who had been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (F06.7) were eligible.

candidate_explanations.difference: Features: P-50 uses VBM subcortical volume, vertex-based shape and SBM sulcal depth/gyrification. P-99 uses 906 FreeSurfer morphometric features reduced by chi-squared SelectKBest, with grid-searched classifiers.
candidate_explanations.quote: We obtained 906 non-null features after all steps, including the voxel count, number of vertices, surface area of various brain structures, and thicknesses and curvatures of cortical areas.

candidate_explanations.difference: Scanner and site: a 3T Philips Achieva in Nanjing against a 1.5T Toshiba in Moscow.
candidate_explanations.quote: All imaging data were acquired on a 3 T Philips Achieva TX MRI scanner using an 8-channel head coil in Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital.

candidate_explanations.difference: The Moscow cohort and scanner, stated by P-99.
candidate_explanations.quote: T2-weighted images from Toshiba 1.5 T MR scanner were acquired with the following parameters

reason: Both studies classify clinic MCI against controls from structural MRI. Each study's accuracy and AUC lies outside the other's 95% interval, derived with Wilson and Hanley-McNeil: P-50 0.89 [0.770, 0.953] against P-99 0.73 [0.665, 0.785]; AUC 0.89 [0.793, 0.987] against 0.735 [0.666, 0.804]. Neither paper reports a result under the other's condition. Candidate explanations are within-sample feature derivation in the 46-person P-50 study, sample size, MCI definition, feature set and scanner; none is shown to be sufficient. The ledger record misstates P-50 as an ADNI subset, but its two figures (89% LOOCV, 73% 10-fold) are the ones the papers print, so the discrepancy does not rest on the misreading.

quotes.quote: The present study included 24 MCI individuals and 22 normal controls (NCs). All participants were recruited from neurology clinic of Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital.

SVM achieved the best performance when incorporating all cortical and subcortical features with an accuracy of 89 %, sensitivity of 87 %, specificity of 90 %, and AUC of 0.89 for distinguishing MCI from NC.
leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) was selected to evaluate the performance of the classification model
The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI obtained from the «Memory Clinic» (Moscow, Russia).
Due to an imbalanced dataset, for estimation of model performance, we used 10-fold cross-validation with the F1-metric.
the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)
The model shows better recall (0.796) and precision (0.816) for the MCI group compared to recall (0.583) and precision (0.583) for the Control group.
